scope: Read-only extraction of frozen completion audits, short CUDA profiles, and completed same-protocol reevaluation of our unchanged20k checkpoints. This analysis runs no training/inference, remote access, or test trajectory access.

protocol.branches: Three baseline adaptations: A20000 then two independent B branches initialized from the same-method A checkpoint; each B20000 uses a fresh optimizer and full-model fine-tuning. One GPU per baseline method runs A, single and multi sequentially. Ours: resumed A reaches20000, then two B branches train only damping/context in parallel; see its separate training/cost fields.
protocol.reported_error_scope: All future samples 1..32, excluding anchor; NOT error only at the 3.2-second endpoint.
protocol.independence: Multi expands the SAME 64 initial-condition groups over 6 damping values; 384 records are not 384 independent initial groups.
protocol.readout: Each checkpoint independently calibrates uniform kNN on train fit288 groups and selects k from [1,5,25,50] on disjoint train select96; fit-only feature/target standardization; same readout for teacher and autonomous prediction. Calibration uses physical labels but world-model training/prediction does not.

teacher_gate.meaning: Teacher re-encodes true causal histories. Failure indicates representation/readout is inadequate; autonomous physical metrics for that group are diagnostic, not a clean dynamics ranking.

protocol.stop_definition: 10-frame sliding velocity windows. Truth RMS >0.1*fit-train omega standard deviation is dynamic; predicted RMS <0.1*truth RMS is stopped. Natural near-rest windows excluded.
protocol.checkpoint_selection: Exact last20000, not best validation checkpoint
protocol.cuda_profile: NVIDIA L40, float32 baseline implementations, batch32; warmup3 plus measured10 updates per horizon. Memory is peak within these profiling windows, NOT a monitored peak over the actual 20k training job. Reserved memory includes allocator cache; allocated memory is tensor memory.

core_and_adaptation.native_core: LeHami HamiltonianPredictor: learned separable K(p/s)+V(q,u), leapfrog; no damping
core_and_adaptation.adaptation: q32/p32 by default; full21 history momentum correction added to official causal-last4 SG, zero-initialized output; shared architecture across A/B
core_and_adaptation.objective: official multistep q and SG-p MSE, differentiable targets, joint q,p SIGReg weight .25; frame-unit momentum
core_and_adaptation.readout_features: complete current phase [q,p], including inferred initial correction
core_and_adaptation.batchnorm_boundary: per-raw-time encoder/projector BatchNorm; no future statistics in initializer

core_and_adaptation.native_core: original lucas-maes/le-wm JEPA, ARPredictor, Embedder, MLP and SIGReg
core_and_adaptation.adaptation: LeHami-author ConvEncoder replaces original ViT; latent64 replaces original192; attention context21 replaces3; matched 64x64 RGB
core_and_adaptation.objective: native one-step teacher-forced MSE over K shifted21 contexts plus SIGReg weight .09; not LeHami-author multistep LeWM objective
core_and_adaptation.readout_features: last two 64D latents, diagnostic projection; full recurrent state is21 latents; no past action features
core_and_adaptation.batchnorm_boundary: encoder/projector train per raw time; pred_proj pools only matching absolute source times across shifted contexts; replaces official flattened temporal pooling; inference uses fixed running statistics

adaptations: LeHami ConvEncoder replaces original ViT;64px RGB scaled to[-1,1]
21-frame causal GRU windows replace native per-frame perceptual encoding
Previous anchor window repeats its oldest available raw frame once
CNN training BatchNorm is computed separately per raw time index
One matched anchor instead of all sequence starts in the official loss
Native PIC uses observed target phases only in its auxiliary training loss
Inference only encodes initial21 frames; autonomous two-state recurrence
Feature readout uses[s_t,s_t-s_previous], the complete recurrence state
Passive zero actions only;physical dt=.1, native normalized Euler dt=1
Native predictor state-detach behavior preserved;not an official benchmark reproduction

ours.cost_caution: Old launch resumes A from step10000 and then runs the two B branches concurrently using two GPUs. No complete aligned fresh-A20k wall/GPU-hour record or identical short CUDA profile is available here. Do not rank the old job wall time against the single-GPU baseline pipelines; do not substitute old cost estimates.
ours.parameter_count_evidence: CPU construction only of the frozen model class with exact resolved configurations from technical_audit; no optimizer/forward/training. Counts include frozen input_port parameters.
ours.architecture: q2,p2; 4D physical readout; original GroupNorm CNN; H=0.5*p^Tp+V(q), PSD D(q,p,c), frozen discrete-gradient implicit solver with3 nominal substeps/frame. Multi has4D fixed causal context. Encoder/initializer/potential frozen in B.
ours.comparison_boundary: Same-protocol reevaluation controls diagnostics, not architecture, objective, representation dimension, optimizer/trainable parameter budget, or training route. Historical B reports copied the A readout; this reevaluation refits each checkpoint using its own stage training conditions under the common protocol. Do not interpret old-versus-new metric changes as training improvement.
ours.reevaluation_provenance: All three checkpoint SHA256 values exactly match historical completed20k checkpoints; weights unchanged before/after reevaluation; no optimizer and zero world-model updates. Changes from the old report reflect fresh per-checkpoint readout calibration/evaluation protocol, NOT extra training or model improvement.

reliable_findings: All four methods: LeWM has the lowest qualified errors in undamped A. In single b=0.2, LeWM has the lowest angle MAE (.03344rad), while ours has the lowest angular-velocity RMSE (.18548rad/s); ours angle MAE is .03977rad. There is no single winner for both single-condition metrics.

In multi-condition aggregate, ours has the lowest qualified angle MAE (.076485rad) and angular-velocity RMSE (.327343rad/s). This is a single-seed descriptive result under the shared evaluation protocol, not an isolated causal architecture effect.

In multi-condition per-b results, ours leads both metrics at b=.05,.1,.2. At b=0, LeHami leads both; ours angle is worse than both LeHami and LeWM, while ours angular-velocity RMSE lies between them. At b=.5 and1, LeWM leads both and ours is second. These are relative weaknesses, not numerical/stopping failures: ours has full coverage, passes all per-b teacher gates, and has zero detected stop windows.

Among the three external baseline adaptations, LeWM leads A and single on both metrics. Multi aggregate LeHami is modestly better than LeWM; condition-wise LeHami leads b=0,.05,.1,.2 and LeWM leads b=.5,1.

H-JEPA A and multi overall teacher gates fail, so their large autonomous errors and stop flags are diagnostics combining representation/readout and dynamics. H-JEPA single DOES pass; within H-JEPA multi only b=1 passes. Do not label all H-JEPA conditions invalid or treat its failed-gate rows as clean dynamics rankings.
Ours, LeHami and LeWM have zero detected stop windows in all stages under the stated10-frame criterion. This is not proof of long-term physical accuracy.

All nine baseline checkpoints complete20000 updates with audited source/data identity; ours reuses its three previously completed20k checkpoints exactly. All12 validation rollouts have100% coverage. This demonstrates completion/integrity, not multiple-seed generality or8-second future accuracy.

H-JEPA has the fewest baseline parameters but about twice the observed pipeline time; LeWM has the largest measured allocated profile memory. Ours is substantially smaller, but its incomplete old A cost record, restricted B training and two-GPU branch execution prevent a valid full-cost or memory ranking.

The three ours reevaluations use no optimizer, zero world-model updates and unchanged weights. Evaluation protocol hashes, protocol dictionaries, stage data hashes, calibration fit/select pairs and independent group splits match every baseline exactly. New B readouts replace the old frozen-A readout; any old-report metric change is a diagnostic protocol change, not a training gain.
fairness_limits: All named baselines are official-core matched visual/history adaptations, not reproductions of the original paper configuration or task. Retained core components and modifications are recorded above.
One training seed0 and64 independent validation initial groups only. Repeated damping records do not increase independent sample count; no significance/general superiority claim.
Latent losses have different scales, dimensions and objectives. Never compare their numeric magnitude as a performance leaderboard.
LeWM uses native one-step teacher-forced shifted-context training, LeHami multi-step phase loss, H-JEPA pH+Bures+PIC; same data/updates do not imply same objective or compute budget.

LeWM readout uses its last two latents (128D), a diagnostic projection of a21-latent recurrent context; LeHami uses complete q/p64D, H-JEPA its complete two-state64D, ours q/p4D. Identical kNN fitting rules do not make feature geometry/capacity identical.

Angular-velocity NRMSE denominators are train-fit standard deviations specific to the stage/calibration set; compare physical RMSE across stages. Stage-specific teacher thresholds are diagnostic policy.

CUDA peaks and per-step times are short fresh-initialization profile measurements, not whole-job resource telemetry; pipeline wall includes setup, I/O, validation and physical evaluation. Allocation/runtime policies are documented.

Ours A is an exact continuation from10k and B trains only damping/context; baselines B fine-tune all modules. Equal final checkpoint steps plus common reevaluation do not isolate a pure integrator or damping-structure effect.
